title: Treasury balance check counts the fee twice
description: The fee is deducted from amountWei, but withdrawEth requires the balance to cover amountWei + feeWei. Withdrawals that the treasury can fully pay revert with InsufficientFunds.

title: Cancelling a withdrawal leaves its id consumed
description: deleteWithdrawMessage clears the message's startTime but not withdrawMsgIdProcessed[withdrawId], so a cancelled withdrawal id can never be authorized again and the contract state is inconsistent.

title: Zero fee receiver is not handled consistently
description: validWithdrawMessage accepts a zero feeReceiver, while Treasury.withdrawEth always tries to pay the fee to it. Either reject a zero fee receiver when authorizing or handle it in the treasury.

title: claimWithdrawal updates state after the external call
description: claimWithdrawal calls Treasury.withdrawEth, which sends ether to the destination, before setting startTime[messageHash] = NEVER. The state update should come before the external call (checks-effects-interactions) to rule out reentrancy.

title: Unused variables
description: Several variables, including Treasury's StorageV1 and some role constants, are never used and should be removed.

title: Authorization does not check withdrawMsgIdProcessed
description: _authorizeWithdraw only rejects a message whose hash already exists; it does not check withdrawMsgIdProcessed, so the same withdrawal id can be reused in a different message.
